evidence.c3: Origins, cross-field evidence, causes and response all present; Bayesian/context causes and most reforms (preregistration detail, larger samples) missing from both scenes.

evidence.c5: Labels accurate (36-50% psychology, ~11% cancer); c1 'Science's growth fuels publish or perish' links to an '[edit]' block (spya-x52rky).

evidence.c1: Origins -> evidence -> two cause bundles -> three response columns matches the article's architecture.
evidence.c2: Overview pairs psychology -> 'publishing rewards positive results' and other fields -> 'weak power' as if each field caused a specific cause family; unsupported pairing.
evidence.c3: Causes zoom covers nine cause sections incl. Bayesian and context sensitivity; responses zoom covers result-blind review, preregistration, p<0.005, triangulation, theory revision.
evidence.c4: Clean, labelled columns in both zooms; detail scenes have large uneven gaps but read easily.
evidence.c5: Labels true to text (e.g. 'Public mostly unaware' matches the German survey); opening node links to the title block and a 'See also' note spends space on back matter.

evidence.c1: Problem -> MI/TE -> limit -> PID -> findings -> practical limits -> future is the review's real spine.
evidence.c2: Evidence zoom routes findings into a decision diamond 'Synergy is concentrated, structured' and draws feedforward -> peak-correlation as if derived; four findings arrow into the Caveats note.
evidence.c3: Method and findings well covered; the Summary's closing claim and the analysis-tools section are absent.
evidence.c4: Readable, but the two bands have no visible labels and edges in the findings fan cut across 'Synergy peaks at mid correlation'.
evidence.c5: Block links land on the right sections; the 'Synergy is concentrated' diamond links only to a section heading.

evidence.c1: Funnel from question to PID, fan of findings, limits, and a summary looping back to the opening question fits the piece.
evidence.c2: Overview converges the culture findings into the macaque study as if it followed from them; the macaque work is a separate later study.
evidence.c3: Adds a future-directions zoom (local PID, PhiID) and the Summary; all major sections represented.
evidence.c4: 'Partial Informatio...' hex truncated, and the dashed loop with its 'returns to the opening question' label runs over the findings region.
evidence.c5: Labels accurate (40% neurons / ~88% synergy, ~7% peak); 'Synergy tracks feedforward TE' links to the section intro block rather than its paragraph.

evidence.c1: Problem, tools, their blind spot, PID, findings fan-and-converge, limits, then loop back to a sharpened answer: a reader gets the shape right.
evidence.c2: Findings zoom is titled 'in order' and drawn as a strict ladder where each result leads to the next; the studies are parallel.
evidence.c3: Covers motivation, both measures, PID derivation step by step, redundancy-vs-synergy timescale result, caveats, primates, summary.
evidence.c4: Overview text is small and the second row of finding boxes overlaps the first row; loop line crosses the regions.
evidence.c5: Paragraph-precise block links throughout; 'Rich clubs do most computing' stretches 'synergy' into 'computing'.

evidence.c1: Spine from problem through PID into a fan of findings and out to limits, future and summary reads as this review's shape.
evidence.c2: Devices mostly earned; the 'Underdetermined - pick one piece to define' diamond in the zoom is a mild decision device on an expository step.
evidence.c3: Problem, measures, PID construction, findings, caveats, primates, limits, future and summary all present at a sensible grain.
evidence.c4: Clean and readable, but the dashed PID-framework region overlaps the findings band and region labels are not shown.
evidence.c5: Labels accurate (2.7x, ~88%); 'Lattice atoms computed by Mobius inversion' links to the ordering paragraph (m37w5y) rather than the inversion one.

evidence.c1: Stakes, biases, four arguments converging on 'functionalism looks shaky', two practical risks, soul ending: the essay's shape.
evidence.c2: Zoom names the convergence 'The arguments reinforce each other' where Seth says each 'can stand up by itself'.
evidence.c3: Arguments and ethics have zooms; the temptations section (intelligence vs consciousness, pareidolia) is reduced to two notes.
evidence.c4: Dashed loop runs through 'Brains aren't computers' with its 'loops back' label on top; bands have no visible labels.
evidence.c5: 'Functionalism looks shaky' links to an empty block (spya-uzr60x); 'reinforce each other' drifts from the text.

evidence.c1: Temptations converge on pareidolia, four doubts converge on 'shaky, not disproven', two worries, false-positive risk, embodied-soul close.
evidence.c2: Labels carefully hedged ('not disproven, just unsupported'); temptations zoom chains biases -> projection -> four lures, a little more causal than the prose.
evidence.c3: Three zooms cover temptations, the four arguments with their examples, and the ethical turn.
evidence.c4: Subtitles overlap ellipse borders ('golem to Lemoine's'), several subs truncated, loop line crosses both regions.
evidence.c5: Mostly paragraph-accurate links; the overview conclusion links to the empty block spya-uzr60x.

evidence.c1: Funnel, four-argument converge and a what-to-do fan are recognisable.
evidence.c2: Temptations zoom wires anthropocentrism -> language -> techno-rapture as a causal cascade the essay does not claim; 'Is computation enough?' drawn as a decision diamond.
evidence.c3: Main parts present, but the false-positive asymmetry and 'no test can settle it' are missing.
evidence.c4: Loop line runs through the argument boxes with an overlapping label; overview bands mostly unlabelled; small text.
evidence.c5: 'Seeming-conscious AI' links to the paragraph about real conscious tech (vs0vpj); 'Illusion won't go away' links to the Suleyman quote; 'Fluent talk' sub says 'hype, techno-rapture'.

evidence.c1: Five labelled movements (why it matters, temptations, four arguments, uncertainty, soul) with an echo loop give the essay's shape.
evidence.c2: Temptations zoom caption says the pulls 'reinforce rather than follow from each other' yet draws them as a derivation chain.
evidence.c3: Includes the 'future isn't fixed' turn and the soul ending as well as the core sections.
evidence.c4: Clean and labelled; zoom title truncated ('We conflate intelligence with...') and the echo label sits on a region border.
evidence.c5: 'Conscious-seeming AI is already risky' links to the real-conscious-tech paragraph (vs0vpj); 'illusion persists' links to the Suleyman quote.

evidence.c1: Overview evidence is a seven-box vertical stack; hub and consequences fan are right but the evidence reads as a generic list.
evidence.c2: Consequences zoom chains sampling -> prime counting -> language design as if each led to the next; the article treats them as separate lessons.
evidence.c3: Turing machines, specs, CA, proofs, irreducibility, testing, surprises, maths, practice and the discovery reframe all appear; a 'Thanks' note wastes space.
evidence.c4: Readable; loop line crosses the evidence region with its label overlapping a box.
evidence.c5: Two nodes link to empty blocks (spya-ypka68, spya-q8fg9q); labels otherwise accurate.

evidence.c1: Demonstrations and proofs converge on an irreducibility hub, then fan to implications and loop back: recognisably this piece.
evidence.c2: 'Good language design is the best defense' overstates; Wolfram says the most important thing in practice is seeing inside the computation.
evidence.c3: Demonstration and proof zooms are detailed; the implications (testing, surprises, maths, AI) get no zoom and the AI point is missing.
evidence.c4: Clear, labelled zooms; hub sub truncated ('computational...') and the loop line passes through the proofs region.
evidence.c5: Several links land on empty figure blocks (#27, #72, #81, #89, #154).

evidence.c1: Funnel of examples into the irreducibility claim, then a fan of consequences, matches the structure.
evidence.c2: Consequences zoom captions itself 'side by side rather than ranked' but draws arrows math -> short programs -> neural nets.
evidence.c3: No zoom for the formal-proof section and the 'bug as discovery' close is absent from the overview.
evidence.c4: Clean, uncrowded, no overlaps; reads at a glance.
evidence.c5: Links land on the right paragraphs; one weak link (e8 rule-122 proof card on the rule-122 paragraph only).

evidence.c1: Chain with a genuine provable-or-not fork, then irreducibility, then two strands meeting in the closing thought.
evidence.c2: The yes/no fork is earned by the rule-122 proof vs the failed proof search; chains elsewhere are mild.
evidence.c3: Zooms cover TM bugs, specs, proofs, and the full run of ruliological surprises, math counterexamples, language design and AI.
evidence.c4: Readable and well spaced; overview bands show no label and the detail chains are long.
evidence.c5: Labels exact (8k-1 glitches, 137,356,329 steps, x^105-1); proof nodes link to empty figure blocks.

evidence.c1: Chain from connectionism through mixed selectivity, oscillations, Spatial Computing hub with two explanatory branches, to consciousness: right shape.
evidence.c2: 'All anesthetics cause slow, scrambled waves' and 'Cognition = organized wave dynamics' overstate a paper that says three drugs and 'may arise'.
evidence.c3: Spatial computing and consciousness zooms; the routing problem behind mixed selectivity is missing.
evidence.c4: Key ellipses truncated ('Spatial Computing...', 'waves select &...'); bands unlabelled.
evidence.c5: 'Unlike Higher-Order theories' contradicts the text, which says the framework 'closely aligns' with HOTs.

evidence.c1: Problem -> classical view -> mixed selectivity -> waves -> spatial computing -> analog -> anesthesia -> hybrid -> conclusion matches the paper's chain.
evidence.c2: 'Consciousness = organized, wave-coordinated cortex' turns a hypothesis into an identity; waves zoom routes efficiency -> anesthesia as if derived.
evidence.c3: Spatial and waves zooms good; rival theories reduced to one box and the routing-problem motivation absent.
evidence.c4: Overview regions overlap and 'Synapses store' straddles the region edge; bands unlabelled.
evidence.c5: Labels accurate to the passages (gamma upper layers / alpha-beta deep, 4 species; millimetre scale).

evidence.c1: Problem-answer chain with a side note for rival theories is the paper's shape.
evidence.c2: Conclusion hedged ('an organized, wave-coordinated cortex'); spatial-computing zoom drawn as a strict ladder for parallel explanations.
evidence.c3: Strong mechanism zoom (1/3 of PFC neurons, routing problem); no zoom for the consciousness framework or rivals.
evidence.c4: Overview regions overlap one another and only one is labelled; detail ladders are long but clear.
evidence.c5: Links precise (e.g. ~1/3 PFC neurons -> amx5qf, which says exactly that).

evidence.c1: Labelled stages flow left-to-right within bands then down to anesthesia, hybrid framework and conclusion.
evidence.c2: Consciousness zoom sets the hybrid against 'Rival theories' converging on 'not broadcasting or hot zones', though the paper aligns with HOTs and shares GW themes.
evidence.c3: Spatial and consciousness zooms; mixed-selectivity motivation and traveling-wave detail only in overview.
evidence.c4: Labelled regions, no overlaps, clear reading order.
evidence.c5: Labels true; HOT box ('top-down organization itself is consciousness') sits under 'rival theories', slightly misframed.
